Share of observed area with water in 2024. Permanent water was detected for all 12 months; seasonal water for 1–11 months. These estimates do not establish water quality, available supply or functioning water services.

PermanentSeasonal
AreaWater shareAny water
Sources, calculation and downloads

JRC Global Surface Water v1.5: seasonality in 2024 and long-term occurrence in 1984–2024. Original 0.00025° cells (approximately 30 m) are assigned by pixel centre and weighted by their equal-area size. Edge allocation is approximate; missing observations are excluded and zero is retained. Hexes and analysis geographies are summarised directly from native pixels. Display images are reduced-resolution overviews. Long-term occurrence is a detection frequency, not the same measure as the 2024 water-area share.

ESA WorldCover 2021. The exported 5 km cell compositions are weighted by the area of each cell overlapping the selected boundary. This assumes the mix within a cell is uniform: small sub-districts may have similar estimates and fine local differences are not resolved. Source, geography and calculation

Area estimates from the published 5 km GRDI means. Each hexagon is weighted by its overlap with the selected area and the fraction covered by source data. Values and coverage are assumed uniform within each hexagon; small areas and edges are less precise. The same 0–100 index scale is used for every area. Missing source values are excluded, never treated as zero. These are area averages, not population-weighted estimates. District polygons can overlap and their totals must not be added. The summary above the chart uses the country or whole-study footprint independently of the district rows. Published map geometries differ in area from the original analytical boundaries by less than 0.5%.

08 / Primary-road proximity

Population near primary roads

WorldPop · 2025

Share of each cluster's modelled population within 10 km of its mapped primary-road network. Choose a cluster to compare national sections. Each country percentage uses that country's roads and population within the cluster.

Within 10 kmOutside 10 km

Loading primary-road population…

Sources and calculation

WorldPop 2025 R2025A constrained, UN-adjusted 1 km modelled counts. Uses the complete Primary roads layer already published in each cluster (© OpenStreetMap contributors), not a named project corridor. Roads outside the cluster are excluded. A 10 km buffer in a local azimuthal equidistant projection is dissolved and clipped to the cluster. For a national section, roads are first clipped to that country's territory within the cluster and the resulting buffer is clipped to the same territory. Overlapping road buffers count people once.

Counts are allocated by original-cell overlap area in Mollweide, assuming uniform population within each cell; the raster is not resampled. Shared overlay precision is 1 mm. OCHA COD-AB boundary gaps and overlaps remain unassigned. Missing raster cells stay excluded; valid-valued cell area is not a population coverage percentage. R2025A was released as an alpha product, and the constrained settlement model can omit or misallocate population. Web geometries are simplified by 20 m only for display.

10 km is a chosen analytical width, not an operational standard. This measures straight-line proximity, not travel access, all-season road access, community investment, economic impact or project beneficiaries. The country denominator is the population inside the cluster, not the full national population. This section has its own comparison selector and is independent of the geography controls above.

09 / Local road connectivity

Where do local roads reach towns?

OSM · 27 October 2026

Share of mapped major-road junctions reaching the selected destinations within 10 km along local roads. Compare districts and zones, then click an area to inspect the hexagons on its map.

Loading local road connectivity…

Area · within clusterShare reaching a mapped destinationReaching / all mapped junctions

OSM completeness has not been independently assessed. “Unavailable” means no qualifying mapped junctions were recorded; 0% means no qualifying route to a mapped destination was found. Neither establishes an absence of connections on the ground. Missing roads, missing settlement nodes and settlement classifications can affect these figures.

Source: © OpenStreetMap contributors / Geofabrik, 27 October 2026 (ODbL 1.0); supplied HDX/OCHA and geoBoundaries administrative polygons. Percentages use summed junction counts. The 10 km path limit is a chosen analytical threshold.

Method, geography and interpretation

Junctions are shared OSM nodes incident to major and local roads with at least three statically accessible neighbours. Major roads include motorway, trunk, primary and their links. Directed motor-access paths exclude major roads and include a settlement-to-road snap of at most 250 m, using a 15 km network halo. Cities/towns are OSM place nodes; the alternative includes villages. Raw nodes are not merged into interchanges.

District and country summaries count junction locations inside the existing administrative boundaries and cluster. Routes may leave those areas or cross borders. Hexagons retain their original full-cell values when a district is selected. District percentages are calculated from junction counts, never from the average of hexagon percentages. Where a district has no junctions, its percentage is undefined. Districts differ in size; some Ethiopian admin 2 units are large zones. Clusters overlap and their counts should not be added as unique junctions.

Tiny incidental boundary overlaps covering less than 0.1% of a source admin 2 polygon and containing no junctions are omitted from the comparison, but retained and flagged in the source download. Original polygons assign the junctions; map outlines are simplified for display only. All junctions in this release have an unambiguous district assignment.

Conditional-access roads are excluded. Turn restrictions, live closures, surface condition and all-season passability are not modelled. The measure describes mapped local-road connectivity. It is not a population-access share or a verified measure of feeder-road use. Independent imagery or a road inventory with separate provenance is needed to assess missing mapping.

Sources & limitations

Data sources, licences and limitations

UNDP · Tajikistan–Kyrgyzstan borderlands. Mapping by Hugh Lamarque. Prepared from the supplied QGIS package, 27 October 2026.

Study area

The study includes Sughd Region, Batken region, Nookat district and Osh city. A 5 km buffer on each side of the Osh–Nookat road connects Nookat to the municipality, restricted to their combined bounding envelope and Kyrgyzstan. Only the intersecting parts of Aravan and Kara-Suu are included. Osh city and the approach contribute to all study totals. Sughd is retained for the Tajikistan country office. The programme summary supports links through Osh, Batken, Isfara and Sughd; the ToR focuses on Batken–Kyzyl-Bel–Isfara. The exact extent and approach width are analytical choices, not a programme-prescribed beneficiary boundary. Analytical administrative polygons predate the 2025 agreement; neither they nor the OSM display reference have been verified against its implementation.

Data coverage · GeoJSON · Programme working extent · GeoJSON · Geographic selection · JSON

National borders use one OpenStreetMap reference network, deduplicated by shared boundary-way IDs from the 27 October 2026 extracts. This avoids stacking disagreeing country outlines. The dashed green line marks the working study extent; it is not a national border. Enclave borders remain visible. Continuous data coverage includes enclosed territories, with their source-country attribution retained. Whole-coverage totals include those territories; inclusion does not establish programme eligibility. Names and boundaries do not imply United Nations endorsement or acceptance; this reference has not been verified against the 2025 agreement.

Interpretation

Map and Analysis share the same study area and data. Five-kilometre hexagons are clipped analytical units, measured flat-to-flat (about 21.65 km² for a full cell). Smaller cells do not increase source resolution. Continuous data coverage includes enclosed territories; source NoData remains missing. Source dates describe the inputs, not current operating conditions.
